day3_night_start_2.text: *I took a shower and came out. My phone screen is lit up. Notifications.*

day3_night_sea_msg.text:
*Sea -- 10:02 PM*

{name}, today was fun. Let's go together tomorrow.

day3_night_sea_msg_2.text: *I didn't read it. I put the phone down while brushing my teeth.*

day3_night_sea_msg_3.text:
*1 minute later. Buzz. Sea — 10:03 PM*

Reply before you go to sleep

day3_night_sea_msg_5.text: *A speech bubble with only three dots clings to the bottom of the chat window.*

day3_night_sea_msg_7.text:
*Buzz. Sea — 10:11 PM*

Why aren't you reading my messages?

day3_night_sea_msg_9.text: *6 messages in 13 minutes. The unread bubbles fill an entire screen. The timestamp on the last bubble keeps catching my eye.*

day3_night_sea_msg_10.text: *I flipped the phone face down. It still buzzes.*

day3_night_sea_msg_11.text: *Buzz. Again. I told myself I wouldn't check the screen, but my hand reaches for it.*

day3_night_sea_msg_12.text:
*Sea — 10:19 PM*

You left the window open, right? Air it out before bed

day3_night_sea_msg_13.text: *The window? My thumb stops over the reply button.*

day3_night_sea_msg_14.text: *I look at the window. The curtain is open. It's dark outside. I can't see anything.*

day3_night_sea_msg_15.text: *In the glass window of the building across from me, the small rectangle of my room is reflected.*

day3_night_sea_msg_16.text: *I closed the curtain. Put the phone in the drawer. Closed the drawer.*

day3_night_sea_msg_17.text: *...It buzzes again from inside the drawer.*

day3_night_bleed.text: *I lay down under the covers. Across the ceiling of my unlit room stretches a long band of streetlight seeping through the gap in the curtains.*

day3_night_bleed_2.text: *The photos Yuna showed me keep coming back to mind. The face was the same in all of them—only the name tags differed.*

day3_night_bleed_3.text: *The name tags change, but the small spot near the eye stays in the same place.*

day3_night_bleed_4.text: *Even with my eyes shut, the thirteen photos in front of the school gate rise up in my mind. The hair colors and name tags varied, yet the eyes were identical in every one.*

day3_night_bleed_no_yuna_1.text: *I never made it up to the rooftop. The note inside my desk, the scratched strokes in the locker, and Sea's messages all surface at once.*

day3_night_bleed_no_yuna_2.text: *I memorized the direction of the school staircases before my classmates' names.*

day3_night_bleed_no_yuna_3.text: *The harder I try to trace it, the more gaps appear.*

day3_night_bleed_5.text: *When I close my eyes, the scenes connect in sequence.*

day3_night_bleed_6.text: *The hallway on the first day. My feet turned toward the vending machine before the sign could tell me where to go.*

day3_night_bleed_7.text: *Before I saw the nameplate for the faculty office, my hand was already pointing down the right hallway.*

day3_night_bleed_7a.text: *The yellow anti-slip tape on the second-floor landing. That color felt familiar from the very first day I saw it.*

day3_night_bleed_8.text: *The stroke bending left inside the locker. It's the same angle as the final stroke in my notebook.*

day3_night_bleed_9.text: *Seolhwa's gaze always went to my left hand first, not my right.*

day3_night_bleed_10.text: *Sea never once packed a side dish I hated in her lunchbox.*

day3_night_bleed_10a.text: *Minsu's speech bubble was spelled far too neatly. His profile picture was still the gray default image.*

day3_night_bleed_11.text: *When I try to picture the gate of my old school, white walls appear first. Nothing comes after.*

day3_night_bleed_12.text: *In my old classroom, a faceless teacher stands in front of the white wall and the blackboard. In the seat beside me, only a desk's shadow remains.*

day3_night_bleed_13.text: *I breathed in. The ceiling pattern looked one square closer at a time.*

day3_night_bleed_14.text: ***There is only the phrase 'old school,' and no place attached to it.***

day3_night_bleed_15.text: *I sat up. Sweat beads on my forehead. My hands are shaking. The plastic feel of the name tag still clings to my fingertips.*

day3_night_stat_crack.text: *I lay back down. Closed my eyes.*

day3_night_stat_crack_2.text: *The side-dish compartments Sea arranged for me. Ms. Eunsu's quiet voice. The rim of the cup Nurse Riin held out.*

day3_night_stat_crack_3.text: *Everything faces the same direction: toward where I sit.*

day3_night_stat_crack_4.text: *The space between the bed and the desk looks narrower than usual. It isn't as if the room has shrunk.*

day3_night_stat_crack_4a.text: *I drew a deep breath, but it stopped halfway in.*

day3_night_stat_crack_6.text: *No. Nothing's there. My eyes are just tired.*

day3_night_ft_nightmare.text: *I close my eyes. Images flood through the darkness.*

day3_night_ft_nightmare_2.text: *I'm walking down a hallway. No end in sight. Each step I take — the hallway stretches longer.*

day3_night_ft_nightmare_3.text: *I opened a classroom door. Same classroom. Opened another. Same classroom. Same seats, same people. Same smiles. All looking at me.*

day3_night_ft_nightmare_4.text: *Twelve cramped rows of names fill the blackboard, beginning with Kim Dojin, Park Seojin, and Kim Taeho. Only the bottom line is blank—and that spot is mine.*

day3_night_ft_nightmare_5.text: *I look at the clock. It has stopped. No—the second hand is moving backward.*

day3_night_ft_nightmare_6.text: *A voice from somewhere. Close, far, all around. ...But there's no door out.*

day3_night_wall.text: *I can't fall asleep. After tossing and turning for a long time, I finally drifted off.*

day3_night_wall_2.text: *3 AM. I got up to use the bathroom. My head feels heavy.*

day3_night_wall_3.text: *Without turning on the light, I head toward the bathroom. My feet, treading the cold floor, came to a stop before the wall.*

day3_night_wall_4.text: *In the streetlight bleeding past the curtains, penciled words show faintly on the wall. It's my handwriting.*

day3_night_wall_6.text: *I stopped breathing. I turned on the light. The fluorescent flickers on. The writing becomes clearly visible.*

day3_night_wall_7.text: *When I move closer to the wall, I smell graphite. The smell of a pencil just sharpened.*

day3_night_wall_8.text: *I touched the writing with my hand. Pencil graphite smudges onto my fingertips. This was written recently. It's not a dried mark.*

day3_night_wall_9.text: *I looked at my hands. Right index finger. Clean. ...Left hand. Pencil marks on my left index and middle finger. The first joint of my index finger is blackened.*

day3_night_wall_10.text: *The strokes are left-handed. The letters press down a little more as they move from left to right.*

day3_night_wall_11.text: *I looked around the room. A pencil is lying on the desk. I didn't leave it there earlier. I put it in the drawer. There is a little graphite on the drawer handle, too.*

day3_night_wall_12.text: *The pencil is on the desk and graphite marks the drawer handle. I remember nothing between those two moments.*

day3_night_seolhwa.text: *As I stare at the writing on the wall, a chill creeps across the nape of my neck. The fluorescent light flickers once.*

day3_night_seolhwa_2.text: *Someone is standing in the corner of the room.*

day3_night_seolhwa_3.text: *A chill grazes the tips of my toes. Even when I breathe out, no visible breath forms in the air.*

day3_night_seolhwa_4.text: *Seolhwa—the girl with dark brown hair I saw by the window—is standing in the corner of my room in her school uniform. It is the dead of night, the door is locked, and the entryway motion-sensor light never came on.*

day3_night_seolhwa_4a.text: I didn't hear the front door or any footsteps. How did you get in? I locked the door.

day3_night_seolhwa_4b.text:
*Beneath the fluorescent light, the focus of her wet eyes looks faintly out of alignment.*

Now isn't the time to ask about that. Listen to me first.

day3_night_seolhwa_6a.text: *I can't get a word out. My lips are dry.*

day3_night_seolhwa_7.text: Within five days... you have to get out of here.

day3_night_seolhwa_7a.text:
*Only after her lips close does the sound strike my left ear a beat late.*

Your voice just now—it didn't match your lips.

day3_night_seolhwa_8.text: Before you end up like me.

day3_night_seolhwa_9.text: Like you? What happened to you?

day3_night_seolhwa_10.text:
*Seolhwa's hand reaches out toward my face. Her fingertips halt just shy of my cheek.*

Wait, your shadow—

day3_night_seolhwa_11.text:
*As though my eyes can't hold focus, the outline of her fingertips doubles and wavers. We're right beneath the fluorescent light, yet Seolhwa casts no shadow on the floor.*

Your hand's going blurry. Where are you going?

day3_night_seolhwa_11a.text:
*A wet line on her cheek vanishes when I blink.*

Were you crying? Wait. Don't disappear.

day3_night_seolhwa_13.text: *I blink. The girl is gone. There is nothing where she stood. No footprints on the floor.*

day3_night_seolhwa_14.text: *Only the air where I was standing is cold. The fluorescent light still hums, very low.*

day3_night_seolhwa_15.text: *I walked over to where she had stood and pressed my hand to the floor. Only my own palm is cold; the vinyl flooring is the exact same temperature as the rest of the room.*

day3_night_seolhwa_16.text: *The writing on the wall is still there. 'Get out of here.' I look at my left hand. My pencil-stained fingers slowly curl, then straighten.*

day3_night_seolhwa_17.text: *The wall clock's second hand sounds unnaturally clear. With every tick, my eyes return to the writing on the wall.*

day3_night_seolhwa_18.text: *Between the ticking of the clock, scenes from today cut in out of order.*

day3_night_choice.text: *I opened the drawer and took out my phone, looking back and forth between the writing on the wall and the dark screen.*

day3_night_investigate.text: *The moment I shut my eyes, the scratched strokes I'd come across at school and my own name tag rose up one after another. In my hand, my phone screen is still lit.*

day3_night_investigate_2.text: *I took a photo of the writing on the wall. After the shutter sound, my left hand appeared small at the bottom of the screen.*

day3_night_deny.text: *It's my first week after transferring. When you're tired, even stains on a wall can look like writing.*

day3_night_deny_2.text: *I pulled the covers over myself. Closed my eyes. The writing on the wall lingers behind my eyelids.*

day3_night_deny_4.text: *Even when I shut my eyes, the four characters on the wall refuse to fade.*

day3_night_ghost_ok.text: Will I see her again if I turn off the light?

day3_xover_glitch_1.text: *A flash cuts across my vision, and instead of my room I see a dark school hallway. Outside the windows, April cherry blossoms are in full bloom.*

day3_xover_glitch_2.text: *Someone is standing there. At the end of the corridor. A pale silhouette.*

day3_xover_glitch_4.text: That time too. And before that. Every time.

day3_xover_glitch_6.text: *I opened my eyes. My room. ...Was it a dream.*

day3_night_pressure_seolhwa_1.text: The notification sound on my phone cut off. Only the time on the screen remained the same.

day3_night_pressure_seolhwa_2.text: Seolhwa's voice came from near my left ear. I turned my head, but there was only my shadow on the wall.

day3_night_pressure_seolhwa_3.text: Write down what you heard today. If you hear it again in the morning, this came first.

day3_night_pressure_seolhwa_4.text: I opened the notebook and wrote the date. My left hand grabbed the paper first, causing the page to crumple.

day3_night_pressure_seolhwa_5.text: And who called first. Similar voices don't mean it's the same person.

day3_night_pressure_seolhwa_6.text: I wrote down only the time I'd heard footsteps outside the front door and left the line below blank.

day3_night_pressure_sea_1.text: The sound of footsteps stopped in the hallway before my phone rang. The name Sea appeared on the screen.

day3_night_pressure_sea_2.text: You're still awake. Your light's on.

day3_night_pressure_sea_3.text: Without answering, I looked out the window and saw that a streetlight was on on the opposite wall.

day3_night_pressure_sea_4.text: You don't have to open the door. I only wanted to hear your voice.

day3_night_pressure_sea_5.text: The door handle did not move. Instead, the corner of a white plastic bag was pushed under the door.

day3_night_pressure_sea_6.text: Eat it for breakfast. The eggs are fully cooked. You don't eat undercooked food.

day3_night_pressure_sea_7.text: I'd never said I disliked soft-boiled eggs. Only the call timer kept ticking up in silence.

day3_night_pressure_sea_8.text: Now close the window. The wind gets in.

day3_night_pressure_sea_9.text: When I pressed the end call button, the vibrations stopped in the hallway. The person at the door was looking at the screen.

day3_night_pressure_sea_11.text: A moment later, the vinyl scratched the threshold. The bag remained, and only the sound of footsteps moved toward the stairs.

day3_night_pressure_sea_12.text: I let go of the curtain and, leaving the light on, wedged a chair against the front door.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_1.text: When I saw my homeroom teacher's number on the screen and pressed the call button, a piece of paper moved on the other side of the receiver.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_2.text: Did you lock your door? Don't open it tonight, no matter who comes.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_4.text: At the other end of the line, a pen tip tapped the desk twice.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_5.text: Just don't open up unless I say my name first. Never open the door on a voice alone.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_6.text: When the entrance intercom was turned on, the screen showed a light on the hallway ceiling instead of a human face.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_7.text: Are you outside my door right now, Ms. Eunsu?

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_8.text: Stop looking at the screen. Close the app, too.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_9.text: When I took my phone away from my ear, the safety app notification overlapped below the busy sign. The location has been confirmed.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_10.text: The teacher did not tell me to open the door or hang up the phone.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_11.text: I'll see you in the classroom in the morning. I'll ask you again then.

day3_night_pressure_eunsu_12.text: The intercom screen stayed lit after the call ended, so I held down the power button until it switched off.

day3_night_pressure_riin_1.text: A message came from the health room number asking me to write down what I ate and drank today.

day3_night_pressure_riin_2.text: I started to write down the name of the drink I'd gotten in the nurse's office, then stopped. I pulled out the slip of paper from my bag pocket and unfolded it.

day3_night_pressure_riin_3.text: Don't reply now. Delete what I sent first.

day3_night_pressure_riin_4.text: The sentence immediately above disappears, and only the message “cancelled” remains in the chat window.

day3_night_pressure_riin_5.text: Didn't you send that, Ms. Riin?

day3_night_pressure_riin_6.text: Right away, a phone call came in from Nurse Riin. The moment the call connected, she asked first whether I had shut my window.

day3_night_pressure_riin_7.text: Raise your voice and they'll hear you next door. I'll ask the questions.

day3_night_pressure_riin_8.text: Instead of asking about symptoms, she only asked how much I had drunk earlier today and whether I had a water cup beside me now.

day3_night_pressure_riin_9.text: Every time Nurse Riin fell silent, someone else's footsteps echoed from the other end of the line.

day3_night_pressure_riin_10.text: Tomorrow, drink only what I gave you. Even if someone says it's the same, take it directly from me.

day3_night_pressure_riin_11.text: Just before hanging up, she said my name, but nothing followed.

day3_night_pressure_riin_12.text: I poured the cold water sitting in my cup down the sink and closed the call log on my phone.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_1.text: A file came under the camera-shaped icon. Yuna told me not to open it but to save it first.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_2.text: Sunbae, just save the photos. I can't talk on the phone tonight.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_3.text: When I clicked Save, the transmission indicator stopped for a moment. The number twelfth was added to the end of the file name.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_4.text: Please don't rename the files. I'll explain tomorrow.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_5.text: My phone vibrated once outside the door. My phone was in my hand and the sound was off.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_6.text: As I walked toward the door, one more message came in from Yuna. It read, 'Don't open the front door.'

day3_night_pressure_yuna_7.text: I wrote who it was and then deleted it. A shadow appeared under the porch and then disappeared.

day3_night_pressure_yuna_8.text: Even after turning the phone face down, I checked once more that the file transfer had finished.

day3_history_callback_18.text: There was also a read mark under the unanswered message on the first day. Sea did not bring up the story that day first.

day3_history_callback_19.text: I moved my finger to close the app. I remembered the screen turning on again the first day, so I didn't turn it off this time.

day3_history_callback_20.text: Recalling the file I had seen in the faculty room earlier today, I started to mention the number written before my name, then wrote down the time of the call first instead.

day3_history_callback_21.text: As I copied the characters I had seen in the old building into my notebook, she heard the rustle of paper and asked what I was looking at.

day3_history_callback_22.text: When I started to bring up what I had seen in the nurse's office earlier today, Nurse Riin cut me off and told me not to say that name over the phone.

day3_history_callback_23.text: I tried gauging how much I had drunk earlier using my water cup, but Nurse Riin asked for the exact time I'd last taken a sip rather than the amount.

day3_history_callback_24.text: I touched the pocket where I had kept the copy that Yuna handed me. I wrote down the name of this file first so that it can be placed in the same place.
